finding.claim: Broken authorization on /admin/users/<uid>/ban: require_admin's abort(403) raises an HTTPException, which `except Exception` catches and only logs, so do_ban runs for non-admins. The sibling unban route does not catch it.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user (g.user without is_admin) sends POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged ban operation

trace.note: route entry, uid taken from the URL
except Exception catches the werkzeug HTTPException raised by abort
handler only logs a warning, with no return or re-raise
do_ban(uid) executes regardless of the check result

finding.guards_checked: require_admin does check is_admin, but its exception is swallowed, so nothing is enforced. The unban route (admin.py:26) calls it without a try/except, so it is safe. No other middleware or before_request hook exists in the repo (single file).

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 is wrapped in `except Exception` (admin.py:18), which only logs. No before_request hook, decorator or other middleware exists. admin.py is the only file in the repo.
verdict.reason: abort(403) at admin.py:11 raises an HTTPException, which `except Exception` at admin.py:18 swallows with only a log at admin.py:19, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any authenticated non-admin. The unban route at admin.py:26 has no try/except and is not affected.
